newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch to decide on extra EU summit after UK poll.
newsitem.headline: Dutch to decide on extra EU summit after UK poll.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said on Friday the Dutch would decide in early May, after the British general elections, whether an extra EU summit will be held in Maastricht in May.

"Technically, all preparations have been taken for an extra summit of government leaders, but we do not intend to take a definite decision until early May, shortly after the British election," Wim Kok told a press conference in the Hague.
He added the timing of the British election was not the only reason for the delay in the "go or no-go decision", but did not specify any other reasons.
Earlier on Friday, Kok's spokesman had said the decision on the summit would most likely take place at a meeting of EU foreign ministers in Luxembourg on April 29-30.
The Dutch foreign ministry has cited May 23 as the most likely date for a special summit.
Kok signalled in early March that a special summit was being considered ahead of a scheduled Amsterdam meeting on June 16-17.
EU leaders are then due to agree a new treaty, paving the way for accession talks with a number of ex-communist states from eastern Europe.

The year-long intergovernmental conference (IGC), aimed at wide-ranging treaty reforms to prepare the union for the expansion process, has become bogged down over how to reshape the executive Commission and ensure fair weighting to member states' votes in the decision-making process.
Kok said on Friday he remained confident that the IGC would be finished according to schedule, but said an extra summit appeared necessary to smooth differences.

"We have made good progress, but on major issues, there are still difference of opinions. It is important for the participants to come to a real willingness to close gaps on the road to the Amsterdam summit instead of only at the summit itself," he said.
